Definition: Affordability of mobile broadband data, measured as the cost of a basic mobile data plan (1-2GB) as a percentage of GNI per capita. The UN Broadband Commission target is below 2% of monthly GNI per capita. Affordability is the single largest barrier to internet adoption in Africa.
revision_notes: The originally cited source (a4ai.org) no longer resolves to any content and now shows only a default Apache server page, so it could not be verified directly. The underlying figure was cross-checked via a Connecting Africa article reporting A4AI/ITU pricing data, which confirms Togo's 1GB entry-level mobile data basket cost 15.10% of average monthly income (GNI per capita) in 2020, ranking Togo among the five most expensive countries in Africa for mobile data that year. Searches for a more recent Togo-specific figure in the ITU Affordability of ICT Services 2023/2024 releases did not surface an updated country-level percentage, so the 2020 data point remains the best-supported evidence available. Value Code 1 (Very Expensive, >10% GNI p.c.) is confirmed.
revised_comments: Mobile data in Togo is very expensive relative to income: an entry-level 1GB mobile broadband basket cost around 15.1% of average monthly income (GNI per capita) in 2020, according to A4AI/ITU pricing data, placing Togo among the five most expensive countries in Africa for mobile data at that time.

Definition: Whether the country has established policies, regulations, and programmes supporting off-grid and distributed energy solutions (mini-grids, solar home systems). These are critical for extending ICT infrastructure to unserved areas beyond the central grid.
revision_notes: The original sources cited (rise.esmap.org and ruralelec.org homepages) did not contain Togo-specific detail, so the score was re-verified against country-specific evidence. REN21's GSR 2024 Togo snapshot and AT2ER (Togolese Rural Electrification and Renewable Energies Agency) project pages confirm an active CIZO off-grid solar programme (pay-as-you-go solar home systems targeting up to 2 million people, with 134,431 kits distributed by June 2023) alongside AT2ER-led mini-grid construction across dozens of rural localities, with new tenders and site completions continuing into late 2025 and 2026, funded by the African Development Bank, EU-Africa Infrastructure Trust Fund, the Sustainable Energy Fund for Africa and the Togolese government. This supports a comprehensive, funded, multi-programme framework with ongoing deployment, consistent with Value Code 4. The evidence does not support the maximum Value Code 5 (mature ecosystem with widespread deployment), since solar home system coverage remained a small fraction of its 2 million target as of 2023 and mini-grid rollout is still in active construction/tendering rather than complete.
revised_comments: Togo maintains a comprehensive off-grid and distributed energy policy framework anchored by the CIZO programme, which combines pay-as-you-go solar home systems with tax exemptions and subsidies for rural households, and by AT2ER-led mini-grid construction financed by the African Development Bank, the EU-Africa Infrastructure Trust Fund, the Sustainable Energy Fund for Africa and the government. Deployment is active and ongoing, with mini-grid construction contracts and site completions across dozens of rural localities through late 2025 and into 2026, alongside continued CIZO solar kit distribution.

Definition: The gap between urban and rural electricity access rates. A smaller gap indicates more equitable energy distribution, critical for ensuring ICT infrastructure can serve the whole population, not just cities.
revision_notes: Confirmed via World Bank SDG7 electrification indicators: urban access to electricity in Togo was 95.0% in 2023 (World Bank EG.ELC.ACCS.UR.ZS) and rural access was 30.5% in 2023 (World Bank EG.ELC.ACCS.RU.ZS, via Trading Economics), giving a gap of approximately 64.5 percentage points. This exceeds the 60pp threshold, confirming Value Code 1 (Gap >60 percentage points).
revised_comments: A substantial urban-rural electrification divide persists in Togo. World Bank data show 95.0% of the urban population had access to electricity in 2023, compared with only 30.5% of the rural population, a gap of roughly 64.5 percentage points. This places electricity access firmly in favour of urban centres, despite ongoing rural electrification programmes.
